identity.description: Gradient-boosted decision-tree ensemble; the strong tabular default. Additively fits shallow trees to the gradient of the loss, capturing non-linearities and interactions with minimal preprocessing.

emits.note: classification; well-ranked but often miscalibrated — see calibration placement
via SHAP (Explainer), not native per-row; global importances are native

invariances.why: split points are threshold comparisons; any monotone rescale of a feature yields identical trees
splits depend only on feature ORDER, so log/rank/box-cox of an input cannot change the fit
the default-direction learning sends missing values down a learned branch — no imputation required
the sklearn wrapper requires pre-encoded integers; native categorical support exists but is off by default in this driver
a non-parametric ensemble makes no assumption about the marginal or error distribution
boosting overfits on very small n without heavy regularization; shines from a few thousand rows up
tree predictions are piecewise-constant; outside the training range the prediction is clamped to the nearest leaf

featureStats.why: boosting needs enough rows per feature to avoid overfitting the gradient; low n/p flags a gate toward simpler families
severe imbalance makes accuracy meaningless and shifts the honest metric to PR-AUC/lift and suggests scale_pos_weight
high missingness is where XGBoost's native-NaN handling is an advantage worth citing over impute-then-linear

modelMetrics.why: if a linear model ties the GBT, the added variance/opacity of boosting is not earning its keep — a commit-linear signal
one feature owning most importance is the leakage-dominance signature the promotion gate blocks

placementClaims.why: native-NaN handling makes upstream imputation unnecessary and sometimes harmful (destroys the missingness signal)
monotone-transform-invariant: Yeo-Johnson/log cannot change the split structure
scale-insensitive by mechanism; standardization is wasted compute
the sklearn wrapper needs categoricals encoded to integers/one-hot before fit
